questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires, orders, or releases provider and room locks? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A reschedule moves an appointment to a new time with the same provider and same room. How many distinct locks does withLocks acquire?
choices: Four, one per key generated by keysFor
Two, because duplicate keys are removed before acquiring
One, because provider and room keys are merged
Zero, because the slots are equal and locking is skipped

questions.prompt: A booking acquires `provider:7` and then times out waiting for `room:3`. What does the caller of book() see and what happens to `provider:7`?
choices: An exception propagates and provider:7 stays held
{ ok: false, reason: "conflict" } and provider:7 is released
{ ok: false, reason: "busy" } and provider:7 is released
{ ok: false, reason: "busy" } but provider:7 is released only when its timer fires

questions.prompt: Why does reschedule re-check the existing appointment's providerId and roomId against `current` inside the lock?
choices: The locks taken are derived from the caller-supplied `current`; if the stored appointment has since moved, those locks would not protect its real resources
To avoid an N+1 query in isFree
Because withLocks requires the keys to be verified before release
It is redundant; the lock already guarantees the values match
